note: Thirteen items. Score each honestly - a generous score helps nobody. Most first-pass profiles land in the 30s and 40s. Built for Design Industries team profiles: the DI alignment item scores how the profile presents the company, because every DI profile is a landing page for it.

items.full_marks: States who you help and what changes for them, carries one piece of proof, and is not the job title. Uses the 220 characters, not 60. Names Design Industries or Atlassian Solution Partner once.
First two lines - everything visible before 'see more' - name the reader's problem. No 'passionate about', no third-person bio, no opening with your own name.
Written to one person in second person: their problem, what you do, one number as proof, what to do next (a DI entry point from positioning.md). Under 1,400 characters. Australian English.
Three items: best-performing post, a proof asset (DI case study or di.net.au article), and the way to contact you. Nothing empty, nothing stale.
One line of positioning and one way to reach you. The DI banner from Tejas, or equivalent. Not the default gradient, not a stock skyline.
Face fills roughly 60% of the frame, eyes visible, shot in the last two years, background not distracting.
One line of scope, then two to three outcome bullets with numbers. Duties are not outcomes. Client outcomes anonymised unless the client is approved.
Last two roles detailed, everything older than ten years compressed to a single line each.
Top three skills are the three you want to be hired for and are endorsed. For most of DI that is a mix of Atlassian products and the discipline. The other 47 are noise.
At least three received in the last two years, each naming a specific outcome rather than character.
Posted or commented in the last seven days. An empty activity feed reads as an abandoned profile.
Custom URL, a working di.net.au email or booking link in contact info, and the same handle as your other platforms.

Describes Design Industries as an Atlassian Solution Partner (never Enterprise Partner), spells the offers the way positioning.md does, uses Australian English throughout, and follows the company page.
